about.title: South San Francisco Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: South San Francisco sees a steady stream of injury collisions each year — recent public records show 251 injury crashes and 342 people hurt in a single year, with reported crashes clustering on Friday nights into early Saturday morning. Corridors like US-101, Route 82, Westborough Boulevard, and Grand Avenue carry heavy volume, and that traffic load shows up in the collision counts. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, the period right after matters: photos fade, memories blur, and vehicles get repaired or scrapped before anyone documents the damage. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects injured South San Francisco residents with an independent personal injury attorney who works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. Reaching out early gives an attorney more room to help you preserve what evidence exists and respond carefully to insurance company outreach.

whyChoose.title: Why South San Francisco Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: California's Comparative Fault Rule Works in Your Favor
items.desc: Even if you're partly at fault for a crash on Westborough Boulevard or Grand Avenue, California's pure comparative fault law still allows you to seek compensation reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help make sure fault isn't overstated against you.

items.title: Deadlines Move Faster Than You Think
items.desc: California generally gives injured people two years to file a car accident claim, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Connecting with an attorney sooner protects your ability to file at all.

items.title: What You Say to the Other Insurer Matters
items.desc: Recorded statements requested by the other driver's insurance carrier are not required, and what you say can be used to minimize your claim later. An independent attorney can advise you before you say anything on the record.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a crash in South San Francisco?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your crash involved a city vehicle, Caltrans, or another government entity — which can come up given how much traffic runs through US-101 and Route 82 — that deadline may be as short as six months, so it's worth acting quickly.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: You're not obligated to, and it's usually wise to avoid it until you've spoken with an attorney. Insurance adjusters often ask questions designed to get you to downplay your injuries or accept partial blame. An independent attorney can help you understand what, if anything, you should say.

items.question: What does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost to find out where you stand.
